Answer: D
Reason: The images show progressive collapse (atelectasis) of the right lower lobe, characterized by increasing opacity and volume loss over time. In a clinical context where this progression is highlighted, foreign body aspiration is a classic cause of such unilateral obstructive atelectasis, particularly if mucous plugging or other causes are less likely or have been ruled out. The density measurements in 3c might also hint at a specific composition or associated finding, but the pattern of progressive lobar collapse strongly points to an obstruction like a foreign body.
